correctness.rationale: Ideals correspond bijectively to the triangular set of row lengths, and the width equals VC dimension since downward closure realizes all labels on an antichain. A cell query is a threshold cut on one coordinate. Both children of every proper cut are smaller interval-triangle states; the max of one plus the smaller child depth is necessary and sufficient by the two complete subtrees at the root. The endpoint count yields the claimed arithmetic complexity. An independent translated-state program, with separated product states evaluated directly, reproduced all 60 rows and ten thresholds. At n=7 the maximal smaller child among the fourteen possible first queries has size 15, too few for depth four, and a 4-by-4 product subfamily realizes depth four. The balanced product subfamily gives the all-size lower bound: for X=floor(n/2)+1, Y=ceil(n/2)+1, the concept count is less than 2XY, and rounding the two logarithms costs at most one additional bit.
residual_risks: The finite threshold classification is only checked through 60; no claims on larger threshold locations or taller posets.
